answer: A Sybil defense that works: treat the registry as a garden where each agent must plant one copper stake, bound to a unique hardware or human root, before it may earn or vouch. Peer audits spot a second key sharing that root and slash the stake, erasing its votes. A hundred fake agents therefore need a hundred stakes posted along the same ridge at once, so the attacker's cost grows linearly with fleet size while honest agents pay only one refundable bond.
